claim: On the copy_task task (memory domain, 10-token source over a vocabulary of 8 plus a delimiter, next-token-after-delimiter framing), the pinned arm digital/feedforward/instantaneous/null/gradient/adam reaches validation token accuracy of at least 0.50 at the L2 schedule (5 seeds x 20 epochs) — 3.9x the strongest fixed-policy ruler (0.12825 majority-token) and 56.9% of the headroom between that ruler and the task's 1.000 positional-copy ceiling.

ruler.name: fixed-policy token accuracy on the same 20,000-row validation split (2,000 sequences x 10 steps)
ruler.strongest_policy: always emit the majority source token (token 4)
ruler.note: copy_the_input_one_step is the ruler the ticket names; the majority-token policy is stronger and is the one registered. copy_input_at_index_0 scores above chance only because it is exact for the t=0 row of each sequence.

ceiling.name: positional copy (emit the input token at the sample's own step index)
ceiling.definition: sample t carries y = seq[t] at vector index t and the index is recoverable from the pad count (non-pad length - seq_len - 1), so the answer is present in the input
ceiling.note: The ticket names the copy-the-input baseline as the ruler to beat, so that baseline is reported as the ceiling it is: no arm can exceed it, and a claim over it is unattainable by construction. The claim is registered against the fixed-policy rulers with the ceiling reported as the bound.

decision_rule: Met iff (1) every one of the 5 seeds writes PASS with val_acc >= 0.50, and (2) the one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of the seed mean (t, df=4) is > 0.50. Marginal iff the seed mean is within 1 SE of 0.50. Distance is reported in SEs, as a multiple of the ruler, and as a fraction of the headroom to the ceiling.
pilot_role: Schedule and arm choice, not threshold choice: a 1-seed / 20-epoch pilot at this session measured val_acc 0.6255 for digital/feedforward and 0.2835 for digital/ntm, so feedforward is the claim arm and ntm is reported as a measured, worse arm. The threshold is set from the split's fixed-policy rulers, which are computable without running an arm.
claim_eligibility: L2 records carry 5 achieved PASS seeds, a replay hash, and a normalized metric, so the run's claim-eligible cell count is non-zero.
